subject: Bridge & throttle recalibration for annual uplift
messages:
From: Daniel Wu <daniel.wu@marketcraft.com>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
Cc: ops@marketcraft.com
Date: 2028-07-11T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Hosted API capacity for FY29 uplift

Hey Stephanie / Vanessa —

Thanks again for the demo last week. We ran the numbers with our finance and platform teams and we expect a 2.8x spike in token consumption starting in October driven by a new recommendation surface. We'd like to accelerate our committed capacity and lock in a rate band that avoids steep overage surprises.

High level asks:
- Increase hosted monthly commit from current 1.2B tokens to 3.5B tokens (phased).
- Prefer a staircase annual term (12 -> 24 months) with mid-term re-eval in 6 months.
- Soft throttle / burst cushions to protect peak traffic during Black Friday.

Can you share a short MOP (mutual action plan) and a quote we can route to procurement? Attaching our traffic profile.

Thanks,
Daniel
Daniel Wu
Head of Platform Engineering, MarketCraft

Attachments: marketcraft_traffic_q2_2028.csv (csv)
From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.com>
To: Daniel Wu <daniel.wu@marketcraft.com>
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-07-11T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Hosted API capacity for FY29 uplift

Thanks, Daniel — great context and congrats on the roadmap lift. We can absolutely design a staged commit uplift with ramped billing bands and a burst cushion for seasonal peaks. I've sketched a 3-phase proposal and attached a short proposal + SOW for procurement review.

Quick summary of our proposal (attached):
- Phase 1 (Oct–Dec): raise to 2.0B monthly commit, 1.25x burst pocket for sudden spikes.
- Phase 2 (Jan–Mar): move to 2.8B monthly commit, introduce throughput-aware soft throttle rules to protect tail latency.
- Phase 3 (after Q1 review): finalize 3.5B commit and convert burst pocket to reserved capacity if stability metrics meet SLAs.

Operational notes: Ben (cc) will run the capacity plan for Dedicated pools and Karthik will confirm any rate-limit implications for shared-hosted SKU routing. Vanessa — I'll need your pricing approval on the stepped discounts for multi-period commits.

Next steps I propose:
1) We send the attached PDF proposal to procurement (DocuSign-ready).
2) Karthik sends an ops checklist for onboarding and a short runbook for soft-throttle behavior.
3) Procurement returns PO or redlines — target the week of 7/24 so we can lock Oct capacity.

I'll follow up with a one-pager MOP for your execs. If that timeline works for you, I'll drop a DocuSign and loop in our finance lead.

Best,
Stephanie Nguyen
Head of Strategic Accounts — Redwood Inference

Attachments: MarketCraft_Redwood_Proposal_July2028.pdf (pdf), SOW_MarketCraft_2028.xlsx (xlsx)
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>, Daniel Wu <daniel.wu@marketcraft.com>
Date: 2028-07-12T10:18:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Hosted API capacity for FY29 uplift — ops & rate notes

Stephanie — adding operational constraints and what we'll do from the runtime side.

Notes:
- Kernel seating & autoscale: for a 3.5B commit we recommend reserving an initial Dedicated buffer of 4 GPUs per region (us-west/us-east) and enabling cross-region burst routing.
- Soft throttle rules: we'll apply per-route percentile latency SLOs; when sustained 95th p95 > 450ms for 5m, requests move to an elevated-cost tier (fall back model variant) for 10m and we notify via webhook. This protects tail latency while keeping throughput.
- Rate bands: stepping discounts require us to pin an initial rate profile. Suggested: 12–24 month commit = 18% unit discount at 2.8B, 22% at 3.5B. Ben, confirm this aligns with pricing model.

Ops checklist (high level):
1) Provision reserved capacity + burst pool. 2) Configure KV-prefix caching for heavy recommendation prefixes. 3) Activate request-level tracing for first 72 hours of Oct. 4) Run a load test during staging window (9/20–9/24).

I will circulate a short ops MOP by EOD 7/13.

—Karthik
